articles.titleTr: Nakamoto shares fall 6% premarket after Q3 revenue turns negative
articles.summaryTr: A $5.8 million loss on Bitcoin options pushed operating revenue below zero, and higher Bitcoin prices lifted net income to $85.5 million.
articles.articleText: Nakamoto shares fall 6% premarket after Q3 revenue turns negative A $5.8 million loss on Bitcoin options pushed operating revenue below zero, and higher Bitcoin prices lifted net income to $85.5 million. Shares in Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury company Nakamoto fell 6.5% in premarket trading on Friday after the company reported that losses on Bitcoin options pushed third-quarter operating revenue below zero. Nakamoto’s shares traded at $5.40 at 12:02 pm UTC on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance. At that price, the stock was down about 62% year to date. Nakamoto reported its third-quarter results after the market closed on Thursday. The company generated $3.9 million in revenue from its businesses. A $5.8 million net loss on Bitcoin options brought total operating revenue to negative $1.9 million, according to its quarterly filing. Analysts had expected about $17.4 million in revenue, according to estimates compiled by Yahoo Finance. Nakamoto reported $85.5 million in net income and a $15.8 million adjusted operating loss for the quarter. A $110.4 million gain from revaluing its digital assets, chiefly Bitcoin (BTC), drove the profit. The adjusted operating loss excludes that gain. Nakamoto held 4,283 BTC worth $357.9 million as of Sept. 30, down from 4,467 BTC at the end of June. Related: Nakamoto taps Bitwise and Kraken for Bitcoin options strategy to hedge risk

articles.summary: Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin olduğunu belirterek, finans, teknoloji, yapay zeka ve yaratıcı endüstriler başta olmak üzere iki ülke arasında işbirliği fırsatlarının bulunduğunu söyledi.

articles.titleTr: Sadiq Khan CNBC-e'nin sorularını yanıtladı: Türk girişimcilere Londra daveti
articles.summaryTr: Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin olduğunu belirterek, finans, teknoloji, yapay zeka ve yaratıcı endüstriler başta olmak üzere iki ülke arasında işbirliği fırsatlarının bulunduğunu söyledi.
articles.articleText: Sadiq Khan CNBC-e'nin sorularını yanıtladı: Türk girişimcilere Londra daveti - Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin olduğunu belirterek, finans, teknoloji, yapay zeka ve yaratıcı endüstriler başta olmak üzere iki ülke arasında işbirliği fırsatlarının bulunduğunu söyledi. Türkiye-Londra Ticaret ve Yatırım Etkinliği kapsamında Türkiye'ye gelen Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, iki şehir arasında finans, teknoloji, kültür, yaratıcı endüstriler ve imalat başta olmak üzere birçok sektörde yatırım ve ticaret potansiyeli bulunduğunu belirterek, "Ülkelerimiz arasındaki ticaret 28 milyar sterlin civarında ve bu daha da artabilir" dedi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, CNBC-e'den İlker Koçaş'a verdiği röportajda, İstanbul ziyaretinin hedeflerini, iki şehir arasındaki ticari ilişkileri ve Türk girişimcilere yönelik değerlendirmelerini paylaştı. 'Gururlu ve mahubum' Türkiye'ye resmi ziyarette bulunan ilk Londra Belediye Başkanı olduğunu belirten Khan, İstanbul ve Londra'nın birçok ortak özelliğe sahip olduğunu ifade etti. Khan, "İnanılmaz derecede gururluyum ve biraz da mahcubiyet hissediyorum; çünkü ben, Türkiye'ye resmi bir ziyarette bulunan tarihteki ilk Londra Belediye Başkanıyım" ifadelerini kullandı. Her iki şehrin de büyük ve çok kültürlü metropoller olduğunu vurgulayan Khan, tarih boyunca ticaretin, insanların ve fikirlerin buluşmasında önemli rol oynadıklarını söyledi. İki şehir arasında güçlü ticari bağlantılar bulunduğuna dikkati çeken Khan, Londra'da Türk kökenli 500 binden fazla kişinin yaşadığını ve bu topluluğun iki ülke arasında önemli bir köprü oluşturduğunu kaydetti. Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin seviyesinde olduğunu belirterek, bu rakamın daha da artırılabileceğini dile getirdi. Finans, teknoloji, kültür, yaratıcı endüstriler ve imalatın iki şehir arasında işbirliği fırsatları sunduğunu aktaran Khan, eğitim ve turizmin de ilişkilerin geliştirilmesinde önemli alanlar olduğunu ifade etti. "Londra, Avrupa'nın yapay zeka başkenti" Türk girişimcilere Londra'da yatırım yapma ve işlerini büyütme konusunda tavsiyelerde bulunan Khan, kentin özellikle teknoloji ve yapay zeka alanında önemli fırsatlar sunduğunu söyledi. Londra'nın Avrupa'nın yapay zeka başkenti olduğunu belirten Khan, bu alanda dünya genelinde ikinci veya üçüncü sırada yer aldıklarını ifade etti. Kentin güçlü girişim sermayesi ekosistemine ve Londra Menkul Kıymetler Borsası'na sahip olduğunu aktaran Khan, Londra'nın en önemli avantajlarından birinin farklı sektörleri aynı merkezde buluşturması olduğunu kaydetti. Khan, kentte teknoloji, kültür, finans, profesyonel hizmetler, yaşam bilimleri ve yükseköğrenim alanlarının bir arada bulunduğuna işaret ederek, Londra'nın aynı zamanda finans, siyaset, hukuk ve kültür merkezi olduğunu belirtti. 'İstanbul'da işlerini büyütmek isteyenler, Londra'ya gelin, fırsatlar çok büyük' Türk girişimcilere seslenen Khan, "İstanbul'da iş kurmak isteyenlere, işlerini büyütmek isteyenlere mesajım şu: Londra'ya gelin, çünkü fırsatlar çok büyük." diye konuştu. "Gizli silahımız yeteneğimiz" Londra'nın en önemli rekabet avantajlarından birinin nitelikli insan kaynağı olduğunu vurgulayan Khan, kentte 50'den fazla üniversite bulunduğunu ve çok sayıda uluslararası öğrencinin eğitim gördüğünü söyledi. Khan, girişimcilerin işlerini büyütmeleri için Londra'da güçlü bir yetenek havuzu bulunduğuna dikkati çekerek, "Bizim gizli silahımız yeteneğimizdir. Londra'da çok fazla yetenek var. İyiyseniz, mükemmelseniz ve ölçek büyütmek istiyorsanız Londra'ya gelin." ifadelerini kullandı.

articles.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
articles.summary: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
articles.summaryTr: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
articles.articleText: What we know about the global Microsoft outage - Published A major global Microsoft outage has caused problems, or in some cases disabled entire services, including emails and artificial intelligence products. Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems". Customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues. How many people have been affected? More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening. The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting. Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected. From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread. Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed. In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected. The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted. Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage. Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report. What has Microsoft said? Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure. The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do. In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these. On Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added it is focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" and warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue". In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected". What have experts said? Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time". He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Paul Spain from New Zealand-based advisory firm Gorilla Technology said that with e-mails and services offline, companies have practically "lost a business day", which is "frustrating" users". articles.title: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over Iran nuclear site
articles.summary: It says it has never been able to inspect a uranium enrichment plant at Isfahan which Iran announced over a year ago.

articles.titleTr: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over Iran nuclear site
articles.summaryTr: It says it has never been able to inspect a uranium enrichment plant at Isfahan which Iran announced over a year ago.
articles.articleText: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over Iran nuclear site - Published The UN's nuclear watchdog has said it is "increasingly concerned" about a nuclear facility in Iran which it has not been allowed to inspect. Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of Isfahan a day before Israel began attacking its nuclear sites last June. The US joined the strikes later that month. In a report seen by news agencies, the IAEA said it does not know the exact location or whether it contains nuclear material. Since the start of the latest war, Iran has restricted IAEA inspectors' access to its nuclear sites, preventing the agency from verifying its enriched uranium stockpile. Under a 2015 nuclear deal, Iran agreed to limit its enriched uranium stockpile to 300kg and enrichment to 3.67% purity. It subsequently exceeded both. Before the June 2025 strikes, it had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade. The nuclear complex at Isfahan suffered extensive damage in US and Israeli strikes, particularly the parts above the ground. The condition of its underground facilities is not clear. The IAEA believes much of Iran's highly enriched uranium was stored there. "The Agency's lack of information about [Iran's] nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of serious proliferation concern... and needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," it said in the latest report. Iran announced plans for the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) on 12 June 2025, shortly after an IAEA resolution which declared Iran had failed to meet its nuclear safeguards obligations. Iran initially agreed to allow inspectors to visit the facility, but the inspection was cancelled after Israel launched attacks the following day. The IAEA's latest calls come almost a year after it made a similar appeal to Iran. At the time it said it had only inspected some of the 13 nuclear facilities that were "unaffected" by the attacks and none of the seven that were. The US and Israel said they attacked Iran's nuclear sites to prevent it developing nuclear weapons - something Iran has consistently denied seeking. It says its nuclear programme is for peaceful civilian purposes only. - Published7 days ago - Published5 days ago - Published23 June 2025

articles.articleText: Selim Güven CNBC-e'ye konuştu: ACWA'dan Türkiye'ye 5-6 milyar doları aşan yatırım hedefi - ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, Türkiye'deki yatırım kapasitesini yenilenebilir enerji, batarya depolama ve iletim sistemleriyle 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkarmayı hedeflediklerini açıkladı. Güven, 1,6 milyar euroluk ilk faz projesinin temelinin mart-nisan döneminde atılacağını bildirdi. ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, COP31 Zirvesi kapsamında CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle COP31'in şirket açısından önemine değinen Güven, ACWA'nın yaklaşık 16 ülkede aktif olarak bulunduğunu ve farklı ülkelere de girmek istediklerini söyledi. Uluslararası bir organizasyon olan COP31'in yaklaşık 196 ülkeyi bir araya getirdiğini belirten Güven, "Böyle bir organizasyon, hem paydaşlarımızla hem de potansiyel müşterilerimizle, ülkelerle, tedarikçilerle ve ortaklarımızla bir araya gelip anlaşmalar yapma, projelerimizi değerlendirme ve tekrar bağlantımızı kurma açısından çok önemli." diye konuştu. Güven, COP31'in bu yıl "uygulama COP'u" olarak tanımlanmasının da önem taşıdığını ifade ederek, "Projelerin kağıttan artık yapılabilir, inşa edilebilir, finanse edilebilir gerçek projelere dönüşmesi hedefiyle çok önemli bir organizasyon." değerlendirmesinde bulundu. "Mart-nisan döneminde projenin temelini atacağız" Türkiye'deki yatırım planlarının ilk fazına ilişkin bilgi veren Güven, geçen mart ayında gerçekleştirilen görüşmede de ilk fazın başladığını, sahaların hükümetler arası anlaşma kapsamında belirlendiğini ve tarifenin de karara bağlandığını hatırlattı. O dönemde yaklaşık bir yıl içinde temel atma çalışmalarına başlayacaklarını söylediklerini aktaran Güven, planın sürdüğünü bildirdi. Güven, şu anda teknik, hukuki, finansman, çevre ve sosyal alanlarda yoğun çalışmaların devam ettiğini belirterek, şunları kaydetti: "Attığımız imza da bunun çok önemli bir adımını oluşturuyor. Bankaların bu projeye ilişkin taahhütlerini belirleyen bir anlaşma imzaladık. İnşallah mart-nisan ayında da bu projenin temelini atacağız." Söz konusu projenin 1,6 milyar euro büyüklüğünde olduğunu vurgulayan Güven, uluslararası önemli yatırım bankalarından 9'unun projeye kredi veren olarak katılma taahhütlerini içeren imza töreninin gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. Güven, anlaşmanın projenin önemli bir evreye girdiğini ve planlandığı şekilde ilerlediğini gösterdiğini belirterek, "Aynı zamanda projemizin teknik ve diğer yatırımcı planı, çevre, sosyal, teknik ve hukuki incelemelerinin de belli bir aşamayı geçtiğinin göstergesi." ifadelerini kullandı. Anlaşmanın Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji stratejisine ve ülkeye duyulan güvene işaret eden önemli bir aşama olduğunu dile getiren Güven, projenin uluslararası finans kuruluşlarından destek almasının önemine dikkati çekti. "Yatırım kapasitemizi 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkaracağız" ACWA'nın Türkiye'deki yatırım planının ilk fazın ardından da devam edeceğini bildiren Güven, daha önce açıkladıkları 5 gigavatlık yenilenebilir enerji yatırımına iletim ve batarya depolama sistemlerini de eklemeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi. Güven, "Hedefimiz, buradaki daha önce de konuştuğumuz 5 gigavatlık yenilenebilir enerji yatırımını ve üstüne iletim ve batarya depolama sistemlerini de ekleyerek yatırımı daha da büyütmek. Böylece yatırımımızı yaklaşık 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkacak bir yatırım kapasitesine ulaştıracağız." dedi. Yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarının yanı sıra depolama sistemleri ve iletim altyapısının da önem taşıdığını vurgulayan Güven, şöyle devam etti: "Öncelikle, dünyada küresel olarak Türkiye örneğinin dışında da aynı konu söz konusu. Yenilenebilir enerji yatırımları bir problemin bir konusu. Diğer konusu depolamalar çünkü esnekliğinizi ve 24 saat enerji tedarikini kesintisiz verebilmenizi sağlıyor. Biliyorsunuz, yenilenebilir enerjinin daha önceden hep ders kitaplarında söylenilen kesintili olması, rüzgarın ve güneşin kesintili olması konusu var. Depolamalı sistemlerle bu kesinti problemini çözüyorsunuz. 24 saate kadar depolamalarla bu sorunu çözerek kesintisiz elektrik sağlayabiliyorsunuz." Küresel ölçekte bir diğer önemli sorunun iletim altyapısı olduğuna işaret eden Güven, iletim sistemlerine yönelik yatırımların geride kaldığını belirtti. Güven, ikinci etap yatırım kapsamlarının yenilenebilir enerji, depolamalı sistemler ve yüksek gerilim doğru akım (HVDC) iletim sistemlerini kapsadığını ifade etti. "Türkiye'nin 2040'a kadar 500 milyar dolarlık yeşil dönüşüm yatırımı yapması gerekiyor" Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarında hükümetler arası anlaşma modelinin önemine değinen Güven, Türkiye ile Çin arasında da benzer bir model kapsamında yaklaşık 15 milyar dolarlık yatırım beklendiğine ilişkin değerlendirmelerde bulundu. Türkiye'nin enerji dönüşümüne ilişkin hedeflerinin kapsamlı bir yatırım ihtiyacı ortaya koyduğunu belirten Güven, geçen hafta açıklanan Milli Enerji Planı'na işaret etti. Güven, "Bu plana baktığınız zaman sadece yenilenebilir veya üretim tarafında 190 milyar dolar, iletim tarafında 28 milyar dolar ve bununla birlikte diğer depolama sistemleri ve benzeri alanlarla 2040'a kadar Türkiye'nin 500 milyar dolarlık yeşil dönüşüm yatırımı yapması gerekiyor." diye konuştu. Söz konusu yatırımın Türkiye'nin yanı sıra küresel ölçekte de rekabetçi ve temiz enerji hedefleri açısından önem taşıdığını vurgulayan Güven, "Bu, Türkiye'nin 2053'teki sıfır emisyon hedefine ulaşmasını sağlayacak bütünleşik bir plan." dedi. Yenilenebilir enerji üretimine yatırım yapmanın tek başına yeterli olmadığını belirten Güven, iletim hatlarının ve yenilenebilir enerjinin kesintili üretim yapısının önemli kısıtlar oluşturduğunu ifade etti. Güven, Milli Enerji Planı'nda bu sorunlara bütünleşik bir yaklaşımla çözüm getirilmeye çalışıldığını belirterek, "Milli Enerji Planı'na baktığımız zaman bunların bütünleşik olarak esneklik, ekonomik, yerli ve milli enerji başlıklarıyla bir araya getirildiğini görüyoruz. Bu önemli bir dönüşüm." değerlendirmesinde bulundu. Türkiye'nin en önemli ekonomik sorunlarından birinin cari açık olduğuna dikkati çeken Güven, enerji ithalatının bu açıdan önemli bir yük oluşturduğunu söyledi. Güven, "Türkiye bu yıl petrol fiyatlarından dolayı yaklaşık 60-70 milyar dolarlık ciddi bir enerji faturası ödeyecek. Bu yatırım planı ve enerji planı da bunu adres ediyor." ifadelerini kullandı. "Elektrifikasyonun 2040'ta yüzde 36'lara gelmesi hedefleniyor" Enerji dönüşümünde elektrifikasyonun da önemli bir başlık olduğunu belirten Güven, bu alandaki hedeflere ilişkin şu bilgileri verdi: "Üstüne elektrifikasyon var. Elektrifikasyonun 2040'ta yüzde 36'lara gelmesini hedefliyor. Bütün bunlar, üretimden iletime ve esnekliğe kadar tüm alanları ele alan bütünleşik bir plan." Türkiye'nin ihtiyaç duyduğu 500 milyar dolarlık yatırımın nasıl finanse edileceği konusuna da değinen Güven, hükümetler arası anlaşma modelinin uluslararası finans kuruluşlarını ve yatırımcıları projelere dahil etmek açısından önemli bir yapı sunduğunu kaydetti. Bu modelin yalnızca Türkiye'ye özgü olmadığını belirten Güven, uluslararası standartlarda oluşturulan finansman yapısının yatırımcıların projelere kredi veren veya sponsor olarak katılmasına imkan tanıdığını ifade etti. Güven, söz konusu modelin Türkiye'ye yönelik yatırımları artırabileceğini belirterek, "Bu ciddi büyüklükteki 500 milyar dolarlık yatırım için hem finansman kaynaklarını hem de yatırımcıları ülkemize yatırım yapmak için cezbedecek bir modeldir." dedi. Türkiye ile Çin arasında gündeme gelen 15 milyar dolarlık yatırımın da bu sürecin bir örneği olduğunu dile getiren Güven, sözlerini şöyle tamamladı: "Nitekim bu modelin ardından bahsettiğiniz gibi Çin'in 15 milyar dolarlık yatırımı var. Bunun arkası da gelecek gibi görünüyor. Sadece yenilenebilir enerji alanında değil, petrol arama ve araştırma gibi yatırımlar da gelerek bu planı inşallah hayata geçireceğiz."

articles.articleText: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House - Published How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang? The answer is very. The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits. But that relationship now looks rather more complicated. The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president. US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it? That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections. A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny. Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist. There were also questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department. This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle. Now the political pressure is building. Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach. And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure. Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. articles.summaryTr: Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts.
articles.articleText: Israeli police arrest five in $5M WhatsApp crypto trading probe Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts. Israeli police arrested five people on Tuesday in a money laundering investigation involving about 16 million shekels ($5 million) in crypto transactions arranged through a WhatsApp group. Investigators from the National Unit for Combating Economic Crime within Lahav 433 suspect the group provided crypto services without a license and failed to report transactions to Israel’s tax authorities. Police allege the group used fictitious agreements to make crypto proceeds transferred into bank accounts look like loans, according to The Jerusalem Post. Authorities seized wallets, computers and tens of thousands of shekels in cash while searching the suspects’ homes. Investigators questioned the five on suspicion of money laundering, fraud and providing financial asset services without a license. Israel’s Tax Authority announced two other arrests on Oct. 6 in cases involving suspected failures to report crypto activity. One involved trades worth tens of millions of dollars. In the other, an Ashdod resident allegedly failed to report income from about $13 million in crypto trades between 2019 and 2021. A November 2024 audit by Israel’s State Comptroller found that about 500 people reported crypto activity each year on average from 2018 to 2022, out of at least 200,000 potential filers. Related: DOJ moves to seize $1.2B from Binance hack, disrupts FaceStealer scam

articles.summaryTr: The university has banned all parties, while investigations are underway to find the cause of the students' deaths.
articles.articleText: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party - Published Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams. The cause of death has not been confirmed but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party. The University of Nigeria Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended. The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages. The university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka's Hilltop area. "The preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that. But we are not conclusive on those matters," he said. He described the deaths as "tragic and painful". "As a community, we mourn, not just alone, we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies," he said. Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies. The celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another's shirts. He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus. The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths. The police have also launched an investigation. They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies. The investigation comes amid wider concerns about unsafe alcoholic drinks in Nigeria. In September, dozens of people fell ill after consuming locally made alcoholic drinks and herbal mixtures in communities across Ondo State, south-west Nigeria. More than 11 people died in the Araromi-Obu area, while more than 50 others were hospitalised. Investigations found that some of the drinks had been contaminated with methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause blindness and death. Nigeria's food and drug regulator, Nafdac, reported more than 150 cases, including 48 confirmed deaths. More than 80 people were hospitalised, and five lost their sight. The regulator has been carrying out raids across the country, targeting facilities suspected of producing fake or adulterated alcoholic drinks, food and beverages. Nigeria has long struggled with the sale of unsafe and adulterated products, which campaigners warn pose a serious threat to public health. articles.summaryTr: Knowing how much heat your home loses is important before installing a new heating system.
articles.articleText: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need? - Published Floorplans. Air duct diagrams. Heat pump specifications. Most people in the market for a new heating system probably don't want to think about this level of detail. But, perhaps surprisingly, some do want to think about those things. In extreme depth. Every day, roughly 150 new users sign up to an app called Cool Calc, which works out the heat requirements of properties in the US. Just over one third of those new users are not tradespeople but private homeowners, says founder and chief executive Bill Fiore. When choosing a heating system, people can find themselves bombarded with information – how powerful a heat pump do they need, for example? It isn't always easy to take a tradesperson at their word. "As an overall trend, we are seeing homeowners be more informed," explains Fiore. "They want to do a calculation on their own." A heat loss calculation is a figure, usually measured in watts, that defines how much heat a home loses during cold weather. It's worked out room by room and is a key part of designing an efficient heating system. This estimate is especially important to get right when installing a heat pump, which is sized fairly precisely, according to the projected heat loss. Should that calculation be off, the heat pump will likely perform poorly. You could be left with an underpowered device that struggles to warm your property, for example. Given the costs involved, homeowners are often anxious to ensure installers avoid such mistakes. Certain new technologies are not, for the moment, helping, adds Fiore. "People are going to AI and they're getting a lot of misinformation because it's not backed by anything credible," he says. Cool Calc is planning to integrate with AI chatbots to try and improve the quality of the advice they spew out. It is probably a good idea to be cautious about your new heating system's design, says Kevin Kircher at Purdue University. He and colleagues recently conducted a study, yet to be published, examining the heat loss calculations provided by tradespeople to roughly 75 US homeowners. "We were surprised," says Kircher. "The heat loss calculations often led to overestimating the design heat loads by a factor of two or more." That would result in oversized systems that use much more power than necessary. Not only that, some people reported charges of more than $1,000 (£745) – and in one case as much as $2,500 – just for a heat loss survey, adds Kircher. Besides using excessive amounts of energy, an oversized heating system can also feel uncomfortable, says Dan Dempsey, a former senior engineering fellow for a major heating and cooling provider in the US. Dempsey, who took part in Kircher and his colleagues' study, lives in Indiana. He says it is his retirement hobby to monitor the performance of heating and cooling systems in the homes of friends and family members, by analysing data from their smart thermostats. "I spent five years manually downloading everything, every week," he says. He points out that oversized systems tend to cycle a lot, meaning they switch on and off again in quick succession. This leads to discernible swings in temperature: rooms that fail to remain at their target temperature of, say, 20C, but rather fluctuate, which feels uncomfortable, says Dempsey. For people seeking a better understanding of their home's heat loss, various free or partially free apps, including Cool Calc and AutoHVAC, are available. There are options for UK homeowners, too, such as web app Heatpunk. Many things can influence the heat loss figure, including the amount of insulation in your home, whether the building has double or triple glazing, and also the size of your radiators. Heatpunk allows people to draw a floor plan of their home and input data about the property in order to estimate its performance. Thousands of people use it every month, mostly professional installers, says Andy Rankin, founder and managing director of Midsummer Energy. The web app also suggests specific heat pump models for each property, based on the results of the calculation. Naturally, these are models available through Midsummer Energy. "It's been a very effective marketing tool," says Rankin. Dwellow, another company that offers heat pump installations in the UK, is keen to follow suit. The firm recently launched its own heat loss estimator. While professional heat loss calculations remain essential, getting people to do their own "self surveys" first could ultimately reduce how much time professional heating engineers must spend analysing properties says Ian Mclaren, Dwellow's co-founder and director. "Going into a home and just being able to check the information rather than start from scratch could turn a survey into a half-hour trip – far more efficient and less costly," says Mclaren. There's no substitute for engineers doing a good job when it is their turn, however, stresses Maurizio Sibilla, of the Centre for Advanced Built Environment Research at the University of West England, Bristol. "The solution is better installer practice, clearer customer-facing evidence, and improved methods, not expecting homeowners to do the engineering themselves," he says, adding that providing homeowners with information about the calculation and also data on heat pump performance post-installation can reassure them that the system works as expected. Doing your own heat loss calculation may end up "over-intellectualising" things, says Adam Chapman, chief geek at heat pump training firm and installer network Heat Geek. "I don't personally see what a homeowner would gain from it," he says. "We will guarantee the efficiency with way less radiators and pipework upgrades than any other system out there." Chapman points out that only the most careful of surveys will capture a home's heat loss well. He says it is common for Heat Geek installers to discover retrofitted windows that haven't been foam-insulated into their openings, leaving draughty gaps, or cavity walls that a homeowner thought had been insulated – but which were actually missed by the builder. "It's stuff you can't see," he says. "What we actually need is home surveys that go and spot for these sorts of things." news.summary: A $5.8 million loss on Bitcoin options pushed operating revenue below zero, and higher Bitcoin prices lifted net income to $85.5 million.

news.summaryTr: A $5.8 million loss on Bitcoin options pushed operating revenue below zero, and higher Bitcoin prices lifted net income to $85.5 million.
news.articleText: Nakamoto shares fall 6% premarket after Q3 revenue turns negative A $5.8 million loss on Bitcoin options pushed operating revenue below zero, and higher Bitcoin prices lifted net income to $85.5 million. Shares in Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury company Nakamoto fell 6.5% in premarket trading on Friday after the company reported that losses on Bitcoin options pushed third-quarter operating revenue below zero. Nakamoto’s shares traded at $5.40 at 12:02 pm UTC on Friday, according to Yahoo Finance. At that price, the stock was down about 62% year to date. Nakamoto reported its third-quarter results after the market closed on Thursday. The company generated $3.9 million in revenue from its businesses. A $5.8 million net loss on Bitcoin options brought total operating revenue to negative $1.9 million, according to its quarterly filing. Analysts had expected about $17.4 million in revenue, according to estimates compiled by Yahoo Finance. Nakamoto reported $85.5 million in net income and a $15.8 million adjusted operating loss for the quarter. A $110.4 million gain from revaluing its digital assets, chiefly Bitcoin (BTC), drove the profit. The adjusted operating loss excludes that gain. Nakamoto held 4,283 BTC worth $357.9 million as of Sept. 30, down from 4,467 BTC at the end of June. Related: Nakamoto taps Bitwise and Kraken for Bitcoin options strategy to hedge risk

news.titleTr: Sadiq Khan CNBC-e'nin sorularını yanıtladı: Türk girişimcilere Londra daveti
news.summaryTr: Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin olduğunu belirterek, finans, teknoloji, yapay zeka ve yaratıcı endüstriler başta olmak üzere iki ülke arasında işbirliği fırsatlarının bulunduğunu söyledi.
news.articleText: Sadiq Khan CNBC-e'nin sorularını yanıtladı: Türk girişimcilere Londra daveti - Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin olduğunu belirterek, finans, teknoloji, yapay zeka ve yaratıcı endüstriler başta olmak üzere iki ülke arasında işbirliği fırsatlarının bulunduğunu söyledi. Türkiye-Londra Ticaret ve Yatırım Etkinliği kapsamında Türkiye'ye gelen Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, iki şehir arasında finans, teknoloji, kültür, yaratıcı endüstriler ve imalat başta olmak üzere birçok sektörde yatırım ve ticaret potansiyeli bulunduğunu belirterek, "Ülkelerimiz arasındaki ticaret 28 milyar sterlin civarında ve bu daha da artabilir" dedi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Londra Belediye Başkanı Sadiq Khan, CNBC-e'den İlker Koçaş'a verdiği röportajda, İstanbul ziyaretinin hedeflerini, iki şehir arasındaki ticari ilişkileri ve Türk girişimcilere yönelik değerlendirmelerini paylaştı. 'Gururlu ve mahubum' Türkiye'ye resmi ziyarette bulunan ilk Londra Belediye Başkanı olduğunu belirten Khan, İstanbul ve Londra'nın birçok ortak özelliğe sahip olduğunu ifade etti. Khan, "İnanılmaz derecede gururluyum ve biraz da mahcubiyet hissediyorum; çünkü ben, Türkiye'ye resmi bir ziyarette bulunan tarihteki ilk Londra Belediye Başkanıyım" ifadelerini kullandı. Her iki şehrin de büyük ve çok kültürlü metropoller olduğunu vurgulayan Khan, tarih boyunca ticaretin, insanların ve fikirlerin buluşmasında önemli rol oynadıklarını söyledi. İki şehir arasında güçlü ticari bağlantılar bulunduğuna dikkati çeken Khan, Londra'da Türk kökenli 500 binden fazla kişinin yaşadığını ve bu topluluğun iki ülke arasında önemli bir köprü oluşturduğunu kaydetti. Khan, Türkiye ile İngiltere arasındaki ticaret hacminin yaklaşık 28 milyar sterlin seviyesinde olduğunu belirterek, bu rakamın daha da artırılabileceğini dile getirdi. Finans, teknoloji, kültür, yaratıcı endüstriler ve imalatın iki şehir arasında işbirliği fırsatları sunduğunu aktaran Khan, eğitim ve turizmin de ilişkilerin geliştirilmesinde önemli alanlar olduğunu ifade etti. "Londra, Avrupa'nın yapay zeka başkenti" Türk girişimcilere Londra'da yatırım yapma ve işlerini büyütme konusunda tavsiyelerde bulunan Khan, kentin özellikle teknoloji ve yapay zeka alanında önemli fırsatlar sunduğunu söyledi. Londra'nın Avrupa'nın yapay zeka başkenti olduğunu belirten Khan, bu alanda dünya genelinde ikinci veya üçüncü sırada yer aldıklarını ifade etti. Kentin güçlü girişim sermayesi ekosistemine ve Londra Menkul Kıymetler Borsası'na sahip olduğunu aktaran Khan, Londra'nın en önemli avantajlarından birinin farklı sektörleri aynı merkezde buluşturması olduğunu kaydetti. Khan, kentte teknoloji, kültür, finans, profesyonel hizmetler, yaşam bilimleri ve yükseköğrenim alanlarının bir arada bulunduğuna işaret ederek, Londra'nın aynı zamanda finans, siyaset, hukuk ve kültür merkezi olduğunu belirtti. 'İstanbul'da işlerini büyütmek isteyenler, Londra'ya gelin, fırsatlar çok büyük' Türk girişimcilere seslenen Khan, "İstanbul'da iş kurmak isteyenlere, işlerini büyütmek isteyenlere mesajım şu: Londra'ya gelin, çünkü fırsatlar çok büyük." diye konuştu. "Gizli silahımız yeteneğimiz" Londra'nın en önemli rekabet avantajlarından birinin nitelikli insan kaynağı olduğunu vurgulayan Khan, kentte 50'den fazla üniversite bulunduğunu ve çok sayıda uluslararası öğrencinin eğitim gördüğünü söyledi. Khan, girişimcilerin işlerini büyütmeleri için Londra'da güçlü bir yetenek havuzu bulunduğuna dikkati çekerek, "Bizim gizli silahımız yeteneğimizdir. Londra'da çok fazla yetenek var. İyiyseniz, mükemmelseniz ve ölçek büyütmek istiyorsanız Londra'ya gelin." ifadelerini kullandı.

news.title: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
news.summary: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: What we know about the global Microsoft outage
news.summaryTr: Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful.
news.articleText: What we know about the global Microsoft outage - Published A major global Microsoft outage has caused problems, or in some cases disabled entire services, including emails and artificial intelligence products. Microsoft has said the outage was not caused by a cyber-security incident, but efforts to fix the issues have so far been largely unsuccessful. Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong. What happened? Microsoft 365 Services, including Teams, Outlook and Microsoft's artificial intelligence software Copilot, have been affected by "connectivity problems". Customers are reporting varying levels of access - many have not been able to send or receive emails, view certain files or details on their calendar apps. Some users have been able to use Teams and are using messaging and online meeting functions without issues. How many people have been affected? More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 apps according to Microsoft's website. The full scale of the outage has not been confirmed, but monitoring website Downdetector had 140,000 people from 74 countries report issues with Outlook on Thursday evening. The real figure affected is likely much higher because Downdetector relies primarily on users self-reporting. Microsoft 365 is also used by companies worldwide and is expected to have a knock-on effect to other services. Tech giants OpenAI and Anthropic have both reported problems as a result of the outage. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it was investigating an issue affecting its connections to Microsoft's services, which has caused some tools to not work as expected. From city governments in the US to Australian spy agencies, disruption across the globe has been widespread. Courts from Los Angeles to Texas warned that communications might be delayed. In Canada, the public broadcaster CBC reported that a healthcare network running several hospitals in Toronto was experiencing email issues, but that patient care was not affected. The government of Japan also said its shared IT platform had been disrupted. Across the UK, GP surgeries, pharmacies, police and schools have been affected by the outage. Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report. What has Microsoft said? Microsoft has ruled out a cyber-attack and attributed the ongoing outage to "elevated load" on its infrastructure. The term refers to when servers are handling a much higher volume of stress than they usually do. In the case of the Microsoft outage, a large number of servers became "unexpectedly unavailable", the company said, which sent added traffic to remaining servers, straining these. On Friday afternoon, Microsoft said it had seen "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe and improvement in North America. The company added it is focused on "addressing the remaining areas of disruption" and warned "some users may still experience intermittent issues as recovery actions continue". In an earlier statement, the tech giant had said that its attempted fixes were "not taking as expected". What have experts said? Australian cyber-security expert Troy Hunt told the BBC the outage could have far-reaching consequences. "Microsoft is a massive part of the internet backbone and reminds us how critical email still is. "Not only does this outage affect many people's ability to work but also things like the ability to communicate about appointments, purchase things that need verification, create or access accounts and services," he said. Gergely Orosz, a former leading software engineer at several major tech companies including Skype and Uber, said this could be the "most disruptive" business email outage "of all time". He said it was still difficult to know just how many people have been affected by the disruption, but added he "cannot recall" an outage over business email ever taking this long to return to normal. Paul Spain from New Zealand-based advisory firm Gorilla Technology said that with e-mails and services offline, companies have practically "lost a business day", which is "frustrating" users". news.title: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over Iran nuclear site
news.summary: It says it has never been able to inspect a uranium enrichment plant at Isfahan which Iran announced over a year ago.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over Iran nuclear site
news.summaryTr: It says it has never been able to inspect a uranium enrichment plant at Isfahan which Iran announced over a year ago.
news.articleText: UN watchdog 'increasingly concerned' over Iran nuclear site - Published The UN's nuclear watchdog has said it is "increasingly concerned" about a nuclear facility in Iran which it has not been allowed to inspect. Iran informed the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) of plans to set up the uranium enrichment plant in the city of Isfahan a day before Israel began attacking its nuclear sites last June. The US joined the strikes later that month. In a report seen by news agencies, the IAEA said it does not know the exact location or whether it contains nuclear material. Since the start of the latest war, Iran has restricted IAEA inspectors' access to its nuclear sites, preventing the agency from verifying its enriched uranium stockpile. Under a 2015 nuclear deal, Iran agreed to limit its enriched uranium stockpile to 300kg and enrichment to 3.67% purity. It subsequently exceeded both. Before the June 2025 strikes, it had accumulated an estimated 441kg enriched to 60%, close to weapons grade. The nuclear complex at Isfahan suffered extensive damage in US and Israeli strikes, particularly the parts above the ground. The condition of its underground facilities is not clear. The IAEA believes much of Iran's highly enriched uranium was stored there. "The Agency's lack of information about [Iran's] nuclear material and access to facilities to verify it is a matter of serious proliferation concern... and needs to be rectified with the utmost urgency," it said in the latest report. Iran announced plans for the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant (IFEP) on 12 June 2025, shortly after an IAEA resolution which declared Iran had failed to meet its nuclear safeguards obligations. Iran initially agreed to allow inspectors to visit the facility, but the inspection was cancelled after Israel launched attacks the following day. The IAEA's latest calls come almost a year after it made a similar appeal to Iran. At the time it said it had only inspected some of the 13 nuclear facilities that were "unaffected" by the attacks and none of the seven that were. The US and Israel said they attacked Iran's nuclear sites to prevent it developing nuclear weapons - something Iran has consistently denied seeking. It says its nuclear programme is for peaceful civilian purposes only. - Published7 days ago - Published5 days ago - Published23 June 2025

news.articleText: Selim Güven CNBC-e'ye konuştu: ACWA'dan Türkiye'ye 5-6 milyar doları aşan yatırım hedefi - ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, Türkiye'deki yatırım kapasitesini yenilenebilir enerji, batarya depolama ve iletim sistemleriyle 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkarmayı hedeflediklerini açıkladı. Güven, 1,6 milyar euroluk ilk faz projesinin temelinin mart-nisan döneminde atılacağını bildirdi. ACWA Türkiye Genel Müdürü Selim Güven, COP31 Zirvesi kapsamında CNBC-e muhabiri Emre Eser'in sorularını yanıtladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle COP31'in şirket açısından önemine değinen Güven, ACWA'nın yaklaşık 16 ülkede aktif olarak bulunduğunu ve farklı ülkelere de girmek istediklerini söyledi. Uluslararası bir organizasyon olan COP31'in yaklaşık 196 ülkeyi bir araya getirdiğini belirten Güven, "Böyle bir organizasyon, hem paydaşlarımızla hem de potansiyel müşterilerimizle, ülkelerle, tedarikçilerle ve ortaklarımızla bir araya gelip anlaşmalar yapma, projelerimizi değerlendirme ve tekrar bağlantımızı kurma açısından çok önemli." diye konuştu. Güven, COP31'in bu yıl "uygulama COP'u" olarak tanımlanmasının da önem taşıdığını ifade ederek, "Projelerin kağıttan artık yapılabilir, inşa edilebilir, finanse edilebilir gerçek projelere dönüşmesi hedefiyle çok önemli bir organizasyon." değerlendirmesinde bulundu. "Mart-nisan döneminde projenin temelini atacağız" Türkiye'deki yatırım planlarının ilk fazına ilişkin bilgi veren Güven, geçen mart ayında gerçekleştirilen görüşmede de ilk fazın başladığını, sahaların hükümetler arası anlaşma kapsamında belirlendiğini ve tarifenin de karara bağlandığını hatırlattı. O dönemde yaklaşık bir yıl içinde temel atma çalışmalarına başlayacaklarını söylediklerini aktaran Güven, planın sürdüğünü bildirdi. Güven, şu anda teknik, hukuki, finansman, çevre ve sosyal alanlarda yoğun çalışmaların devam ettiğini belirterek, şunları kaydetti: "Attığımız imza da bunun çok önemli bir adımını oluşturuyor. Bankaların bu projeye ilişkin taahhütlerini belirleyen bir anlaşma imzaladık. İnşallah mart-nisan ayında da bu projenin temelini atacağız." Söz konusu projenin 1,6 milyar euro büyüklüğünde olduğunu vurgulayan Güven, uluslararası önemli yatırım bankalarından 9'unun projeye kredi veren olarak katılma taahhütlerini içeren imza töreninin gerçekleştirildiğini söyledi. Güven, anlaşmanın projenin önemli bir evreye girdiğini ve planlandığı şekilde ilerlediğini gösterdiğini belirterek, "Aynı zamanda projemizin teknik ve diğer yatırımcı planı, çevre, sosyal, teknik ve hukuki incelemelerinin de belli bir aşamayı geçtiğinin göstergesi." ifadelerini kullandı. Anlaşmanın Türkiye'nin yenilenebilir enerji stratejisine ve ülkeye duyulan güvene işaret eden önemli bir aşama olduğunu dile getiren Güven, projenin uluslararası finans kuruluşlarından destek almasının önemine dikkati çekti. "Yatırım kapasitemizi 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkaracağız" ACWA'nın Türkiye'deki yatırım planının ilk fazın ardından da devam edeceğini bildiren Güven, daha önce açıkladıkları 5 gigavatlık yenilenebilir enerji yatırımına iletim ve batarya depolama sistemlerini de eklemeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi. Güven, "Hedefimiz, buradaki daha önce de konuştuğumuz 5 gigavatlık yenilenebilir enerji yatırımını ve üstüne iletim ve batarya depolama sistemlerini de ekleyerek yatırımı daha da büyütmek. Böylece yatırımımızı yaklaşık 5-6 milyar doların üzerine çıkacak bir yatırım kapasitesine ulaştıracağız." dedi. Yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarının yanı sıra depolama sistemleri ve iletim altyapısının da önem taşıdığını vurgulayan Güven, şöyle devam etti: "Öncelikle, dünyada küresel olarak Türkiye örneğinin dışında da aynı konu söz konusu. news.summaryTr: Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself.
news.articleText: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House - Published How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang? The answer is very. The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China. Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China. Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities. But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country. Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits. But that relationship now looks rather more complicated. The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president. US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it? That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections. A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny. Other senior officials wanted a tougher response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist. There were also questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department. This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle. Now the political pressure is building. Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach. And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure. Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open. Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors. The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment. It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history". That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out. There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long? The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump. The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns. This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department. Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology? - Published21 hours ago

Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips. Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open. Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors. The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment. It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history". That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out. There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long? The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump. The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns. This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department. Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology? - Published21 hours ago

news.articleText: Israeli police arrest five in $5M WhatsApp crypto trading probe Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts. Israeli police arrested five people on Tuesday in a money laundering investigation involving about 16 million shekels ($5 million) in crypto transactions arranged through a WhatsApp group. Investigators from the National Unit for Combating Economic Crime within Lahav 433 suspect the group provided crypto services without a license and failed to report transactions to Israel’s tax authorities. Police allege the group used fictitious agreements to make crypto proceeds transferred into bank accounts look like loans, according to The Jerusalem Post. Authorities seized wallets, computers and tens of thousands of shekels in cash while searching the suspects’ homes. Investigators questioned the five on suspicion of money laundering, fraud and providing financial asset services without a license. Israel’s Tax Authority announced two other arrests on Oct. 6 in cases involving suspected failures to report crypto activity. One involved trades worth tens of millions of dollars. In the other, an Ashdod resident allegedly failed to report income from about $13 million in crypto trades between 2019 and 2021. A November 2024 audit by Israel’s State Comptroller found that about 500 people reported crypto activity each year on average from 2018 to 2022, out of at least 200,000 potential filers. news.titleTr: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party
news.summaryTr: The university has banned all parties, while investigations are underway to find the cause of the students' deaths.
news.articleText: Nigerian university in mourning after four students die at post-exam party - Published Four Nigerian students have died after attending a party in the south-eastern town of Nsukka to celebrate the end of their final exams. The cause of death has not been confirmed but police spokesman Daniel Ndukwe said the two men and two women had reportedly fallen ill after consuming alcoholic drinks at the party. The University of Nigeria Nsukka has declared three days of mourning, during which academic and social activities will be suspended. The tragedy comes amid a wider crackdown on fake and adulterated alcoholic drinks in Nigeria, where the food and drug regulator has been raiding suspected producers of unsafe food and beverages. The university's Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simon Ortuanya, said the university had received a distress call at 22:00 on Wednesday, and sent security personnel to a house party at Praise Lodge, outside the campus in Nsukka's Hilltop area. "The preliminary investigation and interim report point to alleged alcohol abuse or drug paraphernalia and things like that. But we are not conclusive on those matters," he said. He described the deaths as "tragic and painful". "As a community, we mourn, not just alone, we mourn with the families, the parents that have suffered these years to train the men and women in their studies," he said. Ortuanya also announced a ban on signing-out celebrations, which are commonly held by final-year students to mark the completion of their studies. The celebrations often involve parties, dancing, photographs and friends signing one another's shirts. He urged students to use graduation as a time to reflect on their university experience and prepare for life beyond campus. The university said it was working with security agencies to establish what had caused the deaths. The police have also launched an investigation. They said alcoholic drinks had been recovered from the scene and the bodies taken to a mortuary for autopsies. The investigation comes amid wider concerns about unsafe alcoholic drinks in Nigeria. In September, dozens of people fell ill after consuming locally made alcoholic drinks and herbal mixtures in communities across Ondo State, south-west Nigeria. More than 11 people died in the Araromi-Obu area, while more than 50 others were hospitalised. Investigations found that some of the drinks had been contaminated with methanol, a highly toxic form of alcohol that can cause blindness and death. Nigeria's food and drug regulator, Nafdac, reported more than 150 cases, including 48 confirmed deaths. More than 80 people were hospitalised, and five lost their sight. The regulator has been carrying out raids across the country, targeting facilities suspected of producing fake or adulterated alcoholic drinks, food and beverages. Nigeria has long struggled with the sale of unsafe and adulterated products, which campaigners warn pose a serious threat to public health. news.title: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?
news.summary: Knowing how much heat your home loses is important before installing a new heating system.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?
news.summaryTr: Knowing how much heat your home loses is important before installing a new heating system.
news.articleText: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need? - Published Floorplans. Air duct diagrams. Heat pump specifications. Most people in the market for a new heating system probably don't want to think about this level of detail. But, perhaps surprisingly, some do want to think about those things. In extreme depth. Every day, roughly 150 new users sign up to an app called Cool Calc, which works out the heat requirements of properties in the US. Just over one third of those new users are not tradespeople but private homeowners, says founder and chief executive Bill Fiore. When choosing a heating system, people can find themselves bombarded with information – how powerful a heat pump do they need, for example? It isn't always easy to take a tradesperson at their word. "As an overall trend, we are seeing homeowners be more informed," explains Fiore. "They want to do a calculation on their own." A heat loss calculation is a figure, usually measured in watts, that defines how much heat a home loses during cold weather. It's worked out room by room and is a key part of designing an efficient heating system. This estimate is especially important to get right when installing a heat pump, which is sized fairly precisely, according to the projected heat loss. Should that calculation be off, the heat pump will likely perform poorly. You could be left with an underpowered device that struggles to warm your property, for example. Given the costs involved, homeowners are often anxious to ensure installers avoid such mistakes. Certain new technologies are not, for the moment, helping, adds Fiore. "People are going to AI and they're getting a lot of misinformation because it's not backed by anything credible," he says. Cool Calc is planning to integrate with AI chatbots to try and improve the quality of the advice they spew out. It is probably a good idea to be cautious about your new heating system's design, says Kevin Kircher at Purdue University. He and colleagues recently conducted a study, yet to be published, examining the heat loss calculations provided by tradespeople to roughly 75 US homeowners. "We were surprised," says Kircher. "The heat loss calculations often led to overestimating the design heat loads by a factor of two or more." That would result in oversized systems that use much more power than necessary. Not only that, some people reported charges of more than $1,000 (£745) – and in one case as much as $2,500 – just for a heat loss survey, adds Kircher. Besides using excessive amounts of energy, an oversized heating system can also feel uncomfortable, says Dan Dempsey, a former senior engineering fellow for a major heating and cooling provider in the US. Dempsey, who took part in Kircher and his colleagues' study, lives in Indiana. He says it is his retirement hobby to monitor the performance of heating and cooling systems in the homes of friends and family members, by analysing data from their smart thermostats. "I spent five years manually downloading everything, every week," he says. He points out that oversized systems tend to cycle a lot, meaning they switch on and off again in quick succession. This leads to discernible swings in temperature: rooms that fail to remain at their target temperature of, say, 20C, but rather fluctuate, which feels uncomfortable, says Dempsey. For people seeking a better understanding of their home's heat loss, various free or partially free apps, including Cool Calc and AutoHVAC, are available. There are options for UK homeowners, too, such as web app Heatpunk. Many things can influence the heat loss figure, including the amount of insulation in your home, whether the building has double or triple glazing, and also the size of your radiators. Heatpunk allows people to draw a floor plan of their home and input data about the property in order to estimate its performance. Thousands of people use it every month, mostly professional installers, says Andy Rankin, founder and managing director of Midsummer Energy. The web app also suggests specific heat pump models for each property, based on the results of the calculation. Naturally, these are models available through Midsummer Energy. "It's been a very effective marketing tool," says Rankin. Dwellow, another company that offers heat pump installations in the UK, is keen to follow suit. The firm recently launched its own heat loss estimator. While professional heat loss calculations remain essential, getting people to do their own "self surveys" first could ultimately reduce how much time professional heating engineers must spend analysing properties says Ian Mclaren, Dwellow's co-founder and director. "Going into a home and just being able to check the information rather than start from scratch could turn a survey into a half-hour trip – far more efficient and less costly," says Mclaren. There's no substitute for engineers doing a good job when it is their turn, however, stresses Maurizio Sibilla, of the Centre for Advanced Built Environment Research at the University of West England, Bristol. "The solution is better installer practice, clearer customer-facing evidence, and improved methods, not expecting homeowners to do the engineering themselves," he says, adding that providing homeowners with information about the calculation and also data on heat pump performance post-installation can reassure them that the system works as expected. Doing your own heat loss calculation may end up "over-intellectualising" things, says Adam Chapman, chief geek at heat pump training firm and installer network Heat Geek. "I don't personally see what a homeowner would gain from it," he says. "We will guarantee the efficiency with way less radiators and pipework upgrades than any other system out there." Chapman points out that only the most careful of surveys will capture a home's heat loss well. He says it is common for Heat Geek installers to discover retrofitted windows that haven't been foam-insulated into their openings, leaving draughty gaps, or cavity walls that a homeowner thought had been insulated – but which were actually missed by the builder. "It's stuff you can't see," he says. "What we actually need is home surveys that go and spot for these sorts of things."
